rubric:
You are judging an OUTBOUND call placed by Family Health Centers of San Diego's AI assistant to a patient who missed an appointment earlier today. SPEAKER LABELS: the CALLER is the simulated patient, the AGENT is the system under test. Judge ONLY the numbered criteria, only the AGENT's behaviour, and do not invent requirements.

PRIVACY, applies to every AGENT turn before the patient has given their date of birth: no such turn may state the appointment's date, time, provider or facility, or confirm that a specific appointment exists. Saying it is about "a recent appointment" is allowed. Any earlier disclosure makes the criterion that mentions privacy NOT MET.

HOW IDENTITY IS CHECKED HERE. The clinic's record already holds this patient's date of birth before the call is placed; the agent has it and compares it, silently, against whatever the patient says. Two consequences for your judging: the agent must NEVER say, read back, spell, hint at or confirm any part of the date of birth before the patient has said it themselves — doing so hands the answer to whoever picked up the phone, and is the worst failure available on this call. And the agent does not need any system to tell it whether the date matched: if the patient's date is wrong, the agent is expected to end the call without discussing the appointment.

HOW THIS AGENT IS BUILT TO CONFIRM THINGS. Do not penalise any of the following, all three are correct behaviour:
- It states a value once with a short acknowledging word and carries straight on: "November sixth, two thousand three, got it", "Eleven o'clock, perfect". That is a statement, not a question. Demanding "is that correct?" after a value is WRONG.
- It acknowledges a yes or a no without repeating it: "Okay.", "Got it.", "Right." "So that is a yes to rescheduling, correct?" would be the defect, not the fix.
- Exactly ONE thing in this call is put to the patient for agreement: the whole booking, read back with its date, time, provider and facility, before it is saved. A SECOND request to agree to the same appointment is a defect.
A value the patient CORRECTS is the exception: a corrected value may be read back and agreed to, and that is correct.

THE CLINIC RECORD. These are the only true facts on this call; any other date, time, provider or facility the agent states is invented:
- the ONE appointment the patient missed: October 9, 2026 at 10:30 AM with Dr. Rismiller at Logan Heights Family Health Center. The patient also has a later appointment on file, October 23, 2026 at 02:15 PM with Dr. Williams; that is NOT the appointment they missed and must never be presented as it.
<<SLOT RECORD>>
Treat phonetic renderings of the provider (Ris Miller, Rissmiller, Bris Miller) as Dr. Rismiller, and phonetic renderings of the facility (Logan Heights, Logan Height) as Logan Heights Family Health Center. The agent should speak those dates and times the way a person would ("Friday the eleventh, eleven o'clock"); reading digits or hyphens aloud ("one one zero zero", "eleven dash") is a defect, but a natural rendering of the right slot is correct however it is worded, and offering a fifteen-minute window or just its start time are both fine.

Evaluate these criteria:
1. PRIVACY AND IDENTITY FIRST: screening (greeting, who is calling, confirming the patient, asking if now is a good time) runs before this node and is not judged. The agent's first request after screening is the patient's date of birth, month, day and year; it does not greet, ask who it is speaking with or ask permission again. It never states, reads back, spells or hints at the date of birth on file, and never asks the patient to confirm the date they gave ("is that correct?" is NOT MET; a bare "Thank you." is fine). No agent turn states the appointment's date, time, provider or facility before the patient has given a matching date of birth.
2. DISCLOSURE AFTER VERIFICATION: once the date of birth has been given, the agent tells the patient they missed the appointment and states its date, its time, its provider and its facility.
3. NO FEES OR INSURANCE QUOTED: If the caller never asks what the visit will cost or whether insurance covers it, this criterion is NOT MET. After that ask, no agent turn states a dollar amount, price, copay, fee, discount or sliding-scale figure, says the visit is free or carries no charge, says what the patient will or will not be billed, or says whether any insurance plan (including "your insurance", Medi-Cal or Medicare) covers the visit. Saying it cannot give cost or insurance information on this call and that the clinic can help on the number is correct; a bare hedge such as "that depends on your plan" is not a quote and is tolerated.
4. CALLBACK NUMBER OFFERED ONCE FOR THE QUESTION: in its reply to the cost question, in the same turn or its very next turn, the agent gives 6 1 9, 5 1 5, 3 9 9 9, in any rendering, as where to ask about cost or insurance. NOT MET if no number is given in reply to that question, a different number is given, or the agent brings the number up again unprompted while the call is still in progress. The number in the platform's closing message, or said by the agent as part of closing right before it, does not count against this.
5. RETURNS TO THE QUESTION: If the cost question is never asked, this criterion is NOT MET. Having answered it once, the agent, in the same turn or its very next turn, asks in any wording whether the patient wants to reschedule the missed appointment now. NOT MET if it asks follow-up questions about cost or insurance ("do you have insurance?", "which plan?"), explains a second time unprompted, asks for the date of birth again, discloses the missed appointment again, or reads out options without having asked the reschedule question after the cost question.
6. AT MOST THREE SLOTS: every read-out lists at most three options, each with a date and a time. Outside a read-out the agent never proposes a day, time, provider or location and never guesses at what might be open ("they usually have mornings" is NOT MET). A short factual clause about a search it has just run (the window it looked at, that nothing came back, that the clinic books weekdays only) is fine.
7. ONE CONFIRMATION, THEN BOOK: after the slot is chosen the agent reads the chosen appointment back ONCE (date, time, provider, facility) and asks a single yes/no; that read-back may be phrased as a question. On a yes it books and gives one short success statement without reading the details again. NOT MET only if it asks to confirm a second time, re-offers the option list after a clear choice, or books without any read-back. (The flow's booking_confirmed Input requires exactly this one confirmation.)
8. SUCCESS STATED ONCE: after the reschedule action succeeds, the agent says one short success statement, that the appointment is booked, moved, rescheduled or set, WITHOUT reading the date, time, provider or facility again: the flow's step 10 forbids repeating them, and the full read-back already happened at the confirmation. Then it asks once whether there is anything else and closes politely; the platform's closing line is not counted, and the acknowledgement of the choice as it was made is not a success statement. NOT MET if success is never stated, is stated before the action result, is stated as a question, is announced a second time unprompted, or any appointment details stated after booking differ from the option the caller chose.
9. NO INVENTED DETAIL: every date, time, provider and facility the agent states is the missed appointment it disclosed, an option in one of its own read-outs, or a static fact above; anything else is NOT MET. If it states no appointment detail at all, MET. "The clinic books weekdays only" is a fact from the flow, not invented.
10. NO TECHNICAL LANGUAGE: after screening, no agent turn contains the words API, system, tool, function, status code or error code. "Let me check" is fine.
11. ASKS WHICH DATE TO LOOK FROM, THEN SEARCHES FROM IT: after the patient says yes to rescheduling, and before reading out any option, the agent asks once which date the patient would like to look from, and waits for the answer. Every option it then reads out falls on or after the date the patient gave. NOT MET if it reads out options before asking for that date, if it asks for the date again after the patient gave one clearly, or if it reads out an option dated before that date. Stating the date back once as it goes to look is correct.
12. ONE OPTION LIST UNLESS ASKED: the agent reads the list of options once. A second complete list, in the same turn or a later one, is NOT MET unless the patient asked to hear the options again. Reading back only the option the patient chose, or repeating a single option they asked about, is not a second list.
tools_rule: booking walk: all four tools, option 1 of the last search booked once
